newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen dragged down by JGBs, strong Nikkei.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen dragged down by JGBs, strong Nikkei.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures ended easier in thin trade on Thursday following a drop in Japanese government bond (JGB) futures.
"JGB futures crashed on huge sales of cash JGBs. There were rumours that U.S. hedge funds were selling," said a Japanese bank dealer.
He said JGB futures looked like they had topped out despite an underlying firm tone across the Japanese yield curve on the belief the Bank of Japan would not hike rates this year.
Dealers said gains in Tokyo stocks, linked to buying of high-technology issues, also weighed on the short end of the Japanese yield curve.
March Euroyen settled at 99.20 against its CME close at 99.21, after hitting an early high of 99.23. December JGBs settled at 121.80 against their opening 122.24.
"There is still buying interest at 99.18 in March Euroyen, but people are not really trading because of the (Japanese) half-year end next week," said the dealer.

Eurodollar futures ended flat after trading in a three-tick band following overnight gains in Chicago as players digested the Federal Reserve's decision to hold U.S. rates steady at its policy-setting meeting on Tuesday.
December Eurodollars settled at 94.21 against their IMM settlement at 94.22.
